approved: Treasury Laws Amendment (Making Sure Foreign Investors Pay Their Fair Share of Tax in Australia and Other Measures) Bill 2019
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill is part of a package that would tighten tax rules for foreign investors in Australia.
The package would increase the withholding tax rate on certain managed investment trust payments to 30 per cent, matching the top corporate rate.
It would also limit tax exemptions for foreign superannuation funds and sovereign entities, and restrict double gearing through thin capitalisation rules.
Raises the managed investment trust withholding rate on non-concessional income to 30 per cent.
Limits the withholding tax exemption for foreign superannuation funds.
Codifies and narrows the sovereign immunity tax exemption.
Modifies thin capitalisation rules to prevent double gearing structures.
Improves integrity rules for stapled structures.
Foreign investors in Australian managed investment trusts, stapled structures, and entities claiming sovereign immunity or superannuation fund tax concessions.

The government opposed suspending standing orders, citing important business including the bipartisan passage of strawberry industry legislation, and listed several bills for introduction, such as the Higher Education Support Amendment (VET FEE-HELP Student Protection) Bill 2018 and the Treasury Laws Amendment (Making Sure Foreign Investors Pay Their Fair Share of Tax in Australia and Other Measures) Bill 2018.

The Treasury Laws Amendment (Making Sure Foreign Investors Pay Their Fair Share of Tax in Australia and Other Measures) Bill 2018 was moved to close loopholes allowing foreign investors to use stapled structures and tax concessions to reduce tax on Australian business income, often below 15%. The bill will tax active business income at the corporate rate, limit exemptions for foreign pension and sovereign wealth funds to passive income, and is estimated to gain $400 million in revenue over the forward estimates, with transitional arrangements for existing investments.

The speaker argued that Labor’s policy to remove refundable franking credits would effectively impose a "retirement tax" on a million Australian retirees, stealing their overpaid tax. He noted the Economics Committee is conducting an inquiry into the issue, not opposition policy, and that affected retirees want comprehensive tax reform rather than targeted changes.

The three bills close tax loopholes for foreign investors, particularly stapled structures and double-gearing, which allowed them to pay under 15% tax or nothing on Australian business income while Australian entities pay up to 30%. The measures are expected to raise $400 million over the forward estimates and build on previous actions that have raised about $7 billion in liabilities from multinationals.

The bill closes tax loopholes that allowed foreign investors to pay effective rates below 15% via stapled structures, trust layers, and excessive pension fund exemptions, recouping $400 million over four years. The speaker argued it ensures a level playing field for domestic investors, contrasting coalition tax cuts with Labor's proposed $200 billion in new taxes.

The Treasury Laws Amendment bill was supported to close loopholes allowing foreign investors to pay low tax rates, with $5.6 billion already recovered from multinationals. The speaker also urged Queensland Premier Annastacia Palaszczuk to sign the national health agreement for $8 billion and the Skilling Australians Fund for $240 million.

The bill closing tax loopholes for foreign investors, including stopping double gearing and taxing income from Australian agricultural land and residential property at the top corporate rate, was supported. Personal income tax cuts and the creation of 1.2 million jobs under the coalition government were also highlighted.
The bill neutralises tax benefits from stapled structures used by foreign investors, is estimated to gain $400 million in revenue, and protects the integrity of Australia's corporate tax base.
